az_entrance_boulders.blurb: Entrance Boulders is the first bouldering wall a climber meets in Pima Canyon, on the Phoenix side of South Mountain, a short walk up the wash from the canyon road. It holds 21 problems, all boulders, running from V0 up to V7, with most of the weight between V2 and V6 and a handful of harder lines above that. The canyon has the densest concentration of problems on the mountain and this wall is its busiest corner, so expect company. Quality is mixed: a few standout lines among plenty of forgettable ones, and some tops are crumbly, so check holds before committing to a mantel.
az_entrance_boulders.parking_note: Leave the car in the lot near 48th Street and Guadalupe, then walk the canyon road in. It runs about a mile to a stone ramada on the south side, where you turn southwest up the wash.
az_entrance_boulders.approach: Walk the dirt road into Pima Canyon from the lot for just over a mile, to the ruins of a stone building, then head southwest up Pima Wash for a quarter to half a mile (about 15 minutes); the wall is obvious.

az_davey_jones_locker.blurb: Davey Jones Locker is a boulder cluster in the Oak Flat zone of Queen Creek Canyon in central Arizona, at roughly 3,900 feet. A single large boulder sits in an open spot, undercut and ringed by smaller, less obvious blocks. The 21 problems span V0 to V10, so there is something for most levels: a few easy lines, a solid middle band from V3 to V6, and a short run of difficult problems at the top end. The volcanic rock is abrasive but full of varied holds. Morning sun reaches the main boulder, which makes it a pleasant warm-up on cold days, while some problems on the right stay shaded.

az_rollinstone.blurb: Rollinstone is a small, low-key crag at the top end of the Bear Canyon stretch of the Catalina Highway on Mount Lemmon, near Tucson, at about 6,300 feet. Its 21 routes split roughly evenly between sport and trad, from about 5.6 to the low 5.11s, with the most climbs in the 5.9 to 5.10 range. The wall faces southeast and offers variety in a small space, from slabs to steep roof cracks. Routes here are modest in quality and see little acclaim, so it suits a relaxed day or a few quick pitches rather than a destination trip.

az_wave_area_the.blurb: The Wave Area is a pocket of the Main Boulders at Groom Creek, the hillside bouldering zone south of Prescott, at around 6,200 feet. It has 20 problems, nearly all of them easy: more than half sit at V0, and only a few go beyond V3, with one lone hard problem near the top of the scale. The blocks are coarse, mid-grained granite with sloping and crimpy holds, set among ponderosa pines so the setting is wooded but still sunny. That makes it a friendly spot for newer boulderers and groups, and the rough texture is hard on skin, so tape up.

az_jailhouse_rock.blurb: Jailhouse Rock is the main wall of the Prison Camp area on Mount Lemmon, in the Santa Catalina Mountains outside Tucson, at around 5,000 feet. Its 20 climbs are about evenly split between sport and trad, with a single boulder problem. The focus is on hard lines: most routes fall in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, up to the low 5.13s, while a few easier mixed lines sit around the corner to the left. The rock is smooth and water-polished, which gives the wall a steady, technical feel. It suits strong climbers more than beginners.

az_downtown.blurb: Downtown is the south-of-the-fence half of West Elden, a dacite cliff of about 80 feet on Mount Elden just north of Flagstaff, at roughly 7,000 feet. All 20 routes are trad, spread from easy fifth class through the 5.10s, with a few at 5.11 and one harder line, and they cover cracks, slabs, corners and faces. The dacite is sharp and rough, giving superb friction that can be tough on hands and rope. The wall gets morning shade and afternoon sun, so it works as a summer option, though Flagstaff weather swings widely in spring and fall.

az_totem_proto_area.blurb: Totem-Proto Area is a section of Lower Devil's Canyon within Queen Creek Canyon near Superior, at about 3,600 feet. Its 20 routes mix trad and sport, mostly trad, from the 5.7s to 5.11, with the bulk at 5.9 and 5.10. A two-pitch spire gives the area its name, and newer lines have been added around it in recent years. Climbers describe the rock as good quality with long lines. Because the walk-in and approach are demanding, Lower Devil's Canyon sees far fewer people than the better-known crags nearby, so it tends to feel quiet and committing.

az_west_end_wall.blurb: West End Wall is a tall basalt cliff on the south side of Volunteer Canyon in the Sycamore Canyon country south of Flagstaff, at around 6,600 feet. Its 20 routes are mostly trad and all hard, from about 5.10 into the low 5.13s, with the heaviest concentration at 5.12. The wall is made of tall, twisted columns streaked with black water stains and yellow lichen, and the lines are long and striking. It faces northwest and stays shaded through the morning. The canyon is remote, blocky and often dirty, and the wind can be strong, so expect an adventurous, uncrowded day.
